exposure: excessive weekly gestational weight gain (> 0.49 kg/week)
minimal weekly gestational weight gain (< 0.16 kg/week)
Women delivering preterm (≥ 20 weeks) and at term (≥ 36 weeks)
Gestational weight gain (GWG) according to the 2009 Institute of Medicine guidelines (below, within, or above)
moderate weekly gestational weight gain (0.16-0.49 kg/week)
Rate of GWG (kg/week; minimal [< 0.16], moderate [0.16-0.49], or excessive [> 0.49])
cohort: Obese women (5,651 delivering at ≥ 36 weeks and 6,663 delivering at ≥ 20 weeks)
finding: Excessive gestational weight gain (GWG) in obese women was associated with worse perinatal outcomes, including increased cesarean section, gestational hypertension, and macrosomia, while limited GWG was associated with increased spontaneous preterm birth and SGA infants.
